ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC=4$, $D$ and $E$ are the midpoints of $AB$ and $AC$ respectively. Line $CD$ is drawn, and through point $E$, line $EF\parallel DC$ intersects the extension of $BC$ at point $F$. $DE=CF$, if $\angle B=60^\circ$, what is the length of $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB=AC$ and $\angle B=60^\circ$ \\
it follows that $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle \\
Hence, $BC=AB=4$ \\
Given $D$ is the midpoint of $AB$ \\
it follows $\angle BDC=90^\circ$ and $BD=\frac{1}{2}AB$ \\
Thus, $BD=2$ \\
Therefore, $CD=\sqrt{BC^{2}-BD^{2}}=\sqrt{4^{2}-2^{2}}=2\sqrt{3}$ \\
Since quadrilateral $DCFE$ is a parallelogram \\
it follows that $EF=CD=2\sqrt{3}$ \\
Thus, the length of $EF$ is $\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; BC is extended to the right to F. Point D is located on side AB, point E is located on side AC; the figure draws segment CD, and the segment EF from E to F is in the same direction as CD, indicating EF ∥ DC. D and E are respectively located at the midpoint positions of AB and AC, therefore after connecting DE it is parallel to the base BC, and F is on the extension of BC, so CF and BC are collinear. Reasoning: From the given information AB=AC=4, and ∠B=60°. Because AB=AC, ∠B=∠C; thus ∠C=60°, and then from the sum of the interior angles of a triangle, ∠A=60°, so △ABC is an equilateral triangle, BC=4. D is the midpoint of AB, therefore BD=2. In an equilateral triangle, the segment from C to the midpoint D of AB is a median, and also an altitude, so CD ⟂ AB, and △BDC is a right triangle. Therefore CD=sqrt(BC^2-BD^2)=sqrt(4^2-2^2)=sqrt(12)=2sqrt(3). Also because E is the midpoint of AC and D is the midpoint of AB, DE ∥ BC; and F is on the extension of BC, so DE ∥ CF. Combining the figure and the given information EF ∥ DC, it can be known that quadrilateral DCFE is a parallelogram, therefore EF=DC=2sqrt(3).
